homepage.thumbnailAlt: Crossed wrench and screwdriver over an industrial workshop badge

landing.quickStartText: The first jobs look easy. Then the warning lights, measurements, and mystery faults start stacking up.

footer.aboutText: This fictional, worldwide-friendly challenge uses plain international English, metric measurements, and self-contained workshop rules to explore vehicle knowledge, tool matching, observation, arithmetic, fault logic, communication, and calm judgment. It is for entertainment only and is not mechanical advice, repair instruction, safety guidance, professional training, certification, recruitment screening, or an official mechanic assessment.

stageGroups.title: Workshop Scan
stageGroups.encouragement: Good eye. The tool wall is open now—match each job before the next vehicle rolls in.

questions.prompt: Which component removes excess heat from engine coolant as air passes through it?
questions.explanation: The radiator transfers heat from the coolant to the surrounding air.

questions.prompt: While the engine is running, which component normally supplies electricity and helps recharge the battery?
questions.explanation: The alternator produces electrical power while the engine is operating.

questions.prompt: What does the tread on a tire mainly help it do?
choices: Grip the road and move water
questions.explanation: Tire tread supports grip and channels water away from the contact area.

questions.prompt: A red oil-can symbol appears on the dashboard. Which system is it associated with?
questions.explanation: The oil-can warning symbol is associated with the engine oil-pressure system.

questions.prompt: Which part presses against a brake disc to create friction?
questions.explanation: A brake pad presses against the disc to create slowing friction.

questions.prompt: Which filter cleans air entering the passenger compartment?
questions.explanation: The cabin air filter removes particles from air entering the passenger space.

questions.prompt: Which dashboard instrument records the total distance a vehicle has travelled?
questions.explanation: The odometer records the vehicle's accumulated travel distance.

stageGroups.title: Tool Match
stageGroups.encouragement: Tool choices locked in. Next, prove you can spot the tiny part detail that changes the whole job.

questions.prompt: Which tool is designed to tighten a fastener to a specified turning force?
questions.explanation: A torque wrench is designed to apply a specified amount of turning force.

questions.prompt: Which tool can measure electrical voltage and resistance?
questions.explanation: A multimeter measures electrical values including voltage and resistance.

questions.prompt: A job card asks for the width of a narrow gap. Which tool best matches that task?
questions.explanation: A feeler gauge uses thin calibrated blades to measure narrow gaps.

questions.prompt: Which tool communicates with a vehicle's onboard diagnostic system?
questions.explanation: A diagnostic scan tool reads information from compatible onboard control systems.

questions.prompt: Which hand tool commonly grips a hexagonal nut from several sides?
questions.explanation: A correctly sized socket surrounds and turns a hexagonal fastener.

questions.prompt: Which tool is made to measure the pressure inside a tire?
questions.explanation: A tire pressure gauge directly measures the air pressure in the tire.

questions.prompt: Which item provides broad, stable support for a raised vehicle in a workshop scenario?
questions.explanation: A vehicle support stand is intended to provide stable support at an approved lifting point.

stageGroups.title: Parts & Detail
stageGroups.encouragement: Parts identified. The next bay is all numbers—small differences, exact quantities, no guesswork.

questions.prompt: In a spark-ignition engine, which component creates the spark that ignites the compressed mixture?
questions.explanation: A spark plug creates the electrical spark used to ignite the mixture.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a catalytic converter in an exhaust system?
questions.explanation: A catalytic converter changes several harmful exhaust gases into less harmful substances.

questions.prompt: Why does a differential allow driven wheels to rotate at different speeds?
choices: To help the vehicle turn smoothly
questions.explanation: During a turn, the outer wheel travels farther and needs to rotate faster.

questions.prompt: Which component regulates coolant flow according to engine temperature?
questions.explanation: The thermostat opens and closes to regulate coolant flow as temperature changes.

questions.prompt: A serpentine belt commonly drives which group of components?
questions.explanation: A serpentine belt commonly drives accessories such as the alternator and pumps.

questions.prompt: What does a constant-velocity joint help transmit while allowing steering or suspension movement?
questions.explanation: A constant-velocity joint transmits rotational power through a changing angle.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an electrical fuse?
questions.explanation: A fuse opens the circuit when current exceeds its designed limit.

stageGroups.title: Measure & Ratio
stageGroups.encouragement: Numbers checked. Now the workshop tests whether you can keep every step in the correct order.

questions.prompt: Four wheels each use five fasteners. How many wheel fasteners are there altogether?
questions.explanation: Four wheels multiplied by five fasteners equals twenty fasteners.

questions.prompt: A 3 L mixture uses two parts cleaner to one part water. How much cleaner is required?
questions.explanation: Three total parts equal 3 L, so two parts equal 2 L.

questions.prompt: A measured gap is 0.8 mm and the target is 0.6 mm. How much larger is the measured gap?
questions.explanation: Subtracting 0.6 mm from 0.8 mm gives a difference of 0.2 mm.

questions.prompt: Three tires read 240 kPa and one reads 205 kPa. How far below the others is the lower reading?
questions.explanation: The difference between 240 kPa and 205 kPa is 35 kPa.

questions.prompt: A technician completes three inspection cards per hour. How long will twelve cards take at that rate?
questions.explanation: Twelve cards divided by three cards per hour equals four hours.

questions.prompt: A job requires 5 L of fluid supplied in 1 L containers. How many full containers are needed?
questions.explanation: A total of 5 L divided by 1 L per container equals five containers.

questions.prompt: Checking each of four fasteners takes 30 seconds. What is the total checking time?
questions.explanation: Four checks at 30 seconds each total 120 seconds, which is two minutes.

stageGroups.title: Sequence Control
stageGroups.encouragement: Sequence clean. The easy jobs are over—follow the evidence and find the fault.

questions.prompt: Workshop rule: read the job card, inspect the vehicle, record findings, then report. What comes second?
questions.explanation: The stated sequence places the vehicle inspection immediately after reading the job card.

questions.prompt: A four-step check is A → B → C → D. Step B is complete. Which step comes next?
questions.explanation: In the stated sequence, step C follows immediately after step B.

questions.prompt: Rule: disconnect power before opening the fictional control box. Which order follows the rule?
questions.explanation: The fictional workshop rule explicitly requires power to be disconnected first.

questions.prompt: The job card says: verify part number, fit part, test function, record result. What is the final step?
questions.explanation: Recording the result is the fourth and final step on the stated job card.

questions.prompt: Instruction: if the label is unclear, pause and confirm it before use. The label is unclear. What comes first?
questions.explanation: The instruction says an unclear label must be paused and confirmed before use.

questions.prompt: Steps are numbered 4, 2, 1, 3 on loose cards. Which order restores the intended sequence?
questions.explanation: Sorting the numbered cards in ascending order produces 1, 2, 3, then 4.

questions.prompt: A test must happen after assembly but before sign-off. Which sequence is valid?
questions.explanation: Only assembly, then test, then sign-off satisfies both timing conditions.

stageGroups.title: Fault Finder
stageGroups.encouragement: Fault traced. The next bay tests whether someone else could act on your handover without guessing.

questions.prompt: A lamp does not work. Its fuse and wiring are verified good, but the bulb fails a continuity test. Which item best fits the evidence?
questions.explanation: The failed bulb test is the only confirmed fault among the checked lamp components.

questions.prompt: A fictional pump runs only when connector K is pressed. Power stays present throughout. What clue is most useful?
choices: Movement at connector K changes the fault
questions.explanation: The direct link between connector movement and pump operation is the strongest diagnostic clue.

questions.prompt: Three identical sensors read 20, 20, and 86 under the same condition. Which sensor should be checked first?
questions.explanation: The reading of 86 is the clear outlier under the stated identical conditions.

questions.prompt: A noise appears only while turning left and disappears when stationary. Which note is supported by the evidence?
choices: Noise is linked to left turns
questions.explanation: The observation supports only a connection between the noise and left-turn movement.

questions.prompt: A machine stops after fuse F opens. Replacing nothing, fuse F tests open while every other checked fuse tests closed. What is confirmed?
questions.explanation: The test confirms the state of fuse F but does not establish a deeper cause.

questions.prompt: A rattle stops when an empty metal tray is removed from the vehicle. What is the simplest supported explanation?
choices: The loose tray caused the rattle
questions.explanation: Removing the loose tray immediately removed the symptom, directly supporting that explanation.

questions.prompt: A fault occurs in rain but not in dry tests. Which comparison is most useful next?
questions.explanation: Comparing wet and dry conditions directly tests the one factor already linked to the fault.

stageGroups.title: Clear Handover
stageGroups.encouragement: Handover understood. Now choose the professional workshop decision when the obvious shortcut looks tempting.

questions.prompt: Which handover clearly separates a confirmed fact from an untested possibility?
choices: It is definitely the pump, maybe
Fuse F is confirmed open; the cause is not yet tested
questions.explanation: The statement labels the verified fuse result and keeps the untested cause separate.

questions.prompt: The vehicle is in Bay 4 and the left headlamp is not working. Which update is most precise?
choices: A vehicle has a light problem
questions.explanation: The update gives both the exact location and the specific reported symptom.

questions.prompt: Which note is an observation rather than an assumption?
choices: Voltage measured 10.8 V at connector K
questions.explanation: A recorded measurement is an observation; the other statements add unsupported judgment.

questions.prompt: A replacement part has not arrived. Which handover is clearest?
choices: Part pending; fitting and test remain
questions.explanation: The handover states the blocker and the exact work that still remains.

questions.prompt: A test result changed after connector K was reseated. Which note preserves the useful detail?
choices: Result changed after connector K was reseated
questions.explanation: The precise note records the action and the observed change without overclaiming.

questions.prompt: Which message gives the next technician a useful starting point?
choices: Start by verifying the intermittent signal at connector K
questions.explanation: The message identifies a specific unresolved signal and a clear verification step.

questions.prompt: Which phrase best communicates uncertainty honestly?
questions.explanation: The phrase states the current suspicion while clearly marking confirmation as incomplete.

stageGroups.title: Workshop Judgment
stageGroups.encouragement: Good judgment. The next bay turns up the pace—several jobs, changing priorities, one clear head.

questions.prompt: The job card and the part label show different part numbers. What is the best response?
choices: Fit the part that looks close
questions.explanation: A part-number mismatch should be resolved before the job continues.

questions.prompt: A current service instruction conflicts with an old handwritten note. Which source should guide the fictional task?
questions.explanation: The verified current instruction is the most reliable stated source for the task.

questions.prompt: A required test was skipped, but the result sheet is ready to sign. What is the best choice?
choices: Sign because the sheet is ready
Complete the required test before sign-off
questions.explanation: The required check must be completed before its result can be signed off.

questions.prompt: A measurement is far outside the expected range. What is the strongest first reasoning step?
questions.explanation: Verifying the surprising reading helps separate a true condition from a setup error.

questions.prompt: A customer description is unclear. What is the most useful response?
questions.explanation: A specific neutral question can clarify the symptom without leading the answer.

questions.prompt: Two technicians record conflicting readings from the same point. What should happen next?
choices: Repeat the test with the method confirmed
questions.explanation: Repeating the test with a confirmed method directly addresses the unexplained disagreement.

questions.prompt: A fast shortcut would bypass a stated workshop check. Which choice best protects the quality of the result?
questions.explanation: Following the stated check preserves the evidence needed for a dependable result.

stageGroups.title: Under Pressure
stageGroups.encouragement: Pressure handled. One final repair remains—every clue, number, and handover now matters.

questions.prompt: Two jobs are ready, but Bay A has a confirmed fluid leak and Bay B needs a routine label update. Which should be escalated first?
choices: Bay B because labels are shorter
Bay A with the confirmed leak
questions.explanation: The confirmed leak is the more urgent stated condition and should be raised first.

questions.prompt: The parts desk closes in 10 minutes. A required part number is still unclear. What is the best immediate action?
choices: Wait until tomorrow without noting it
questions.explanation: Verifying the part number addresses the blocker before the stated time limit.

questions.prompt: Three tasks remain: record a completed test, begin a long inspection, and answer an urgent clarification blocking another bay. What should come first?
questions.explanation: The urgent clarification unblocks another bay and can be handled immediately.

questions.prompt: A timer sounds while you are reading a critical job-card update. What is the clearest response?
choices: Acknowledge the timer and preserve the update before switching
questions.explanation: Acknowledging the timer while preserving the critical information avoids losing either task.

questions.prompt: The queue grows, but the latest test contradicts every earlier reading. What should take priority?
questions.explanation: A contradictory test result needs verification before it can support a reliable decision.

questions.prompt: A teammate asks for a status while you are mid-check. Which reply is most useful?
choices: Check in progress; two readings remain
questions.explanation: The response gives a precise current state and quantifies the work remaining.

questions.prompt: A vehicle is ready to leave, but its final result has not been recorded. What is the best action?
choices: Let it leave and reconstruct later
Record and verify the result first
questions.explanation: Recording and verifying the actual result completes the stated workflow before release.

stageGroups.title: The Final Repair
stageGroups.encouragement: Final repair complete. Your mechanic profile is ready for the workshop verdict.

questions.prompt: Final job: the lamp fails only after connector K is moved; the bulb and fuse both test good. Which lead deserves attention first?
questions.explanation: The fault changes directly with movement at K while the other lamp components test good.

questions.prompt: A four-wheel check finds pressures of 235, 235, 205, and 235 kPa. Which reading is the outlier?
questions.explanation: The 205 kPa reading differs from the three matching 235 kPa readings.

questions.prompt: Final sequence: verify identity, inspect, test, report. The vehicle is identified and inspected. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The stated sequence places testing after inspection and before reporting.

questions.prompt: A measured value changes from 12.4 to 9.9 only when load L is connected. Which statement is supported?
choices: Connecting load L is linked to the drop
questions.explanation: The repeated condition directly links connecting load L with the lower measured value.

questions.prompt: The replacement label matches the job card, but the connector shape does not match. What should happen?
questions.explanation: The physical mismatch is unresolved evidence that the part should be verified before use.

questions.prompt: Which final handover is the most complete?
choices: Fault confirmed at K, connection restored, function retested and recorded
questions.explanation: The handover states the confirmed fault, action, retest, and completed record.

questions.prompt: One last contradiction appears after sign-off but before release. What is the strongest workshop decision?
choices: Pause release and resolve the contradiction
questions.explanation: New contradictory evidence should be resolved before the result is treated as complete.
